reviews.text: Wow, This is Awesome! This game gives me Stranded Deep vibes but in Virtual Reality. Note: I was playing using a Quest Pro connected to My PC using a Cable with PD PC Specs: i9-11900K 32GB DDR4 16TB SSD RTX3090 1200W Game Performed Excellent for me. I had ''No'' Issues in My short walk-through. This game doesn't offer much guidance. But, common sense will help you out a lot. for example, first thing I did was get out of the ocean and on to the shore. Right away I noticed a treasure chest with a lock on it. how to open it...? Hmm, Found a Rock and Beat the crap out of the lock and Wow, it worked! I gathered the wood and supplies I needed from the beach to create a fire. Note: The 1st chest I opened had a Torch. Well, before I knew it My Thirst meter is almost empty and there is a voice talking about how I am dying to have a drink. Luckily, I came across some coconuts lying around and again used the stone\rock to break it open. it worked! Now I have to pull of the outer layer off of the coconut. This had me struggling for a minute. I believed, they made it this way on purpose to give you the feel of realism. Pretty Neat! but, a pain in my behind. well, when I first opened it. I was holding the coconut when I went to break it open. Bad Idea! because, as soon as I cracked it open the coconut fell to the ground and all the coconut water spilled out! Well, Dam! Luckily for me there is plenty available. The correct way to open it without spilling would be to hold the coconut with both hands and bang it on the stone/rock that is laying on the ground. doing it this way allowed me to have all the coconut water without spilling a drop. Note: you can still spill it if your'e not careful! So now that I am Good in Health. I started walking around. The daylight was going away fast and I found myself lost in the dark somewhere on the beach. In total darkness some kind of monster attacked me and killed me within seconds. It recorded my death and asked If I wanted to Try Again..? well, Yes! So Now that I have an idea on how it works I stayed in one area of the beach where it starts and just gathered a bunch of wood before it got dark and learned how to make a fire. Note: It was very simple to make a fire. As the Night starts to come in I hear howling and noises like something is running around. I lit up the Torch I got out of the chest and Wow, I am surrounded by four scary looking wolves. Luckily, My Bonfire was going good making it easy to see em and My Torch seems to do a good job of keeping them away. Note: They will try to attack you. but, you can scare them off with the Torch! After awhile. They all turned around and ran away as the daylight was coming. So now that it nice and bright, I went off to explore. Walking around this massive Island. I got lost and went in circles and some how I ended up back on the bench but, in a different area. I found another treasure chest there I broke the lock off and inside this chest was a Pistol, Gun Powder bag, and some Ammo. Note: there were around 13 steel balls that you load in the barrel/muzzle. So first thing I did after picking up and inspecting the gun was I picked up gun powder bag and started pouring some powder into it... I loaded one of the steel balls in to the barrel and turned around to test it out on a crab and as soon as I pulled the Trigger BOOM! a Cloud of Smoke! My Pistol blow up in to pieces. I know because, I see the parts lying on the ground. I believe, I added in way too much gun powder. Well, Dam! This game is Awesome! I will definitely be spending more time in this one. you really feel alone out there. would be nice to have some friends able to join in with ya on your quest. you can explore and do things together. Maybe, someone could of warned me about my mistakes...

This game is NOT WORTH PLAYING in the current state. There's this disgusting bug where the game will infinitely load about 95% of the time I try to launch it, no exaggeration. The loading text will not appear and on the rare case it does, it will load forever. Wouldn't be as big of a deal if the game didn't have this thrilling issue where sometimes the FPS will drop to unacceptable levels and only rise when you relaunch the game. Besides that, the days as everyone else has said, are still too short even after the patch and it leaves very little time to actually get around. The graphics are great, the game is fun, and the physics are great when they work. If only I could play the damn thing without needing to launch it around 30 times to make it playable. UPDATE: Finally launched the game and all of my progress got deleted. Thanks so much for releasing a game in this state and wasting even more of my time. UPDATE 2: This game has a really cool feature where it puts you back at the start every time you finally get it running and that's coupled with an even cooler feature where the game freezes and then you have to relaunch it. Keep up the good work devs.

I realize that this game is early access, but it just feels like less. With the cost at $24 it is a tremendous kick in the jewels to pay that much and get utterly bored with the game because of the brutal day-night cycle. 5min day foraging for stuff to drink and make a fire / 2 min night battling wild dogs?, bats, and jaguars. No thanks, I don't play games to get repeatedly be abused by the core game loop. Supposedly they added fishing in the game? Who has time for that? Don't be ridiculous. What is going on in the developers head. Read all of the reviews... Every one is complaining about this day-night cycle. They said they improved? how bad was it before? I can only imagine that the core loop is the way it is to hide the fact that there is no game. They keep you so preoccupied building fires and bashing coconuts for water you don't have time to see that there is a complete lack of of a game. I'm so disappointed in this game that it nearly seams like fraud. There you have it. Buy this at your own risk. You have been warned. Oh yea, someone said that the performance and graphics are bad. Totally agree. Rocking a 4080 and HP Reverb G2 v2. Horrible. Literally nothing about this game I would consider good at this point. The idea is pretty cool and that is it. Updated Edit based on developer response: Day-Night cycle... I said 5 minutes in jest but developer comment states "around 10". If i estimate ten and then account for a few minutes for sun to go up and down then my in jest statement of it feels like 5 min of day light is all the more real. Wow that is insane. Oh and how does the developer not know the precise timing of day-night when this seams to be a major problem in the game. I know I would know way more than "around 10". I would be out there with the market research quoting times down to the sec. Especially If I'm going to confront a customer with what is actually going on in this game. VR with the Reverb G2... I guess I tested it for you. It works; however, your game is a resource pig at high quality settings. Also, please fix you store listing. If the Reverb is not supported you should not list Steam VR as supportable. To the developer, Your game has a really interesting concept. The idea is really appealing and could be alot of fun. In its current state I cannot recommend. But I am really wanting you to succeed with developing this game. I hope this is not just another VR cash grab which is plaguing the VR marketplace. Good luck!

This game is an absolute SLOG. The stuff they show in the trailers? HA! Good luck getting anywhere near that. 2 hours played and it was just the same boring trek. The only wildlife is Hogs. That's it. Other than that, all you'll ever see is the monsters that come every night. There is a pistol you can find. To defend yourself you say? HA! Its worthless due to the fact you CANNOT carry any more than 2 items, 1 in each hand, and to operate the pistol you have to have: The pistol itself, powder, and shot. THATS 3 ITEMS!! What is even the point of the pistol being in the game! And the worst part about it is when you find the pistol, all the balls are in a nice little box with like 8-10 in there. So its like they show you what you could be using, but because your character is pants on head retarded, you cant use it due to inane carry limitations. I wanted to like the game, its very pretty. But they SERIOUSLY need to revamp the beginning of the game.

games mechanics are good, id chalk the repetitive day / night cycle to just a lack of content as the games still in early access, but i genuinely dont understand unless all the reviews are fake how anyone can ever enjoy this game and play for more than a day. the game is so repetitive and boring everytime id load into a save to do something thinking that maybe i just havent seen enough or i am missing something like finally going to the top of the mountain that the narrator constantly pesters you to do, im met with nothing but dissapointment. Its got to the point where most of my runs end because i just cant be asked anymore doing the same thing over and over and just let myself get eaten by the monsters which are so badly implemented by the way, the game advertises how "realistic" and "immersive" it is but i dont think having 50 monsters swarming you at night at any point of the map is very realistic, like how do they always and instantly know where you are? I understand the creators are just trying to make the nights scarier but it honestly comes through as just annoying and feels like they are picking and choosing with their "realism". Overall, for everyone whos left a bad review aswell as myself i feel we are slightly to blame for expecting a decent actual playable survival game instead of an eating simulator with a day and night cycle. if the devs genuinely want to make a decent game they should stop spending money on fake comments idolising the 60 different things you can do to a coconut and instead try to learn from other games in the genre like the long dark and the way the animals and the world is implemented in there. The devs are genuinely lucky to already have some good ideas, barely any decent competition except from green hell vr which ive heard was abandoned and a pretty sizeable fanbase of AIs so im not too fussed about the 20 quid ive spent as i genuinely think everything is bad just cos its in early access, I look forward to seeing this game progress but as it is right now i wouldnt buy it again if id done the smart thing and not played more than 2 hours thinking it was gonna get better.

From what I can tell, this is a great game that is ruined by one mechanic. I don't see this mentioned anywhere on the store page or reviews so I am going to comment on it here. I am not opposed to the idea of a roguelike survival game, but the way you gain permanent progression is infuriating. I will preface this with the fact that I did not progress far at all. The game is not difficult at all. If you have played survival games, Green Hell (Break coconut) and Don't Starve (Stay near fire at night) specifically, you know what to do to survive and will be able to do so indefinitely as far as I know. I also want you to keep some things in mind as you read so you are aware of the points I am making. - You start with NO INVENTORY, you can only carry an item in each hand. - I believe each day, by default, is about 15 minutes. You will need to survive for 3 days (45 minutes) before you have the CHANCE to FIND a knife. The game's first permanent progression tool. I do some external research and find out you will need to open chests on the beach to get items. This, by itself, is not a problem, I had already opened several because the game is very intuitive (Smash lock with rock to open). I go to open a bunch of chests and do not find anything new, what gives? Apparently you need the chests to respawn to get any new items to spawn in them. This can take up to 10 DAYS (150 MINUTES), OF PLAYTIME FOR THE CHESTS TO RESPAWN SO YOU CAN GET THE FIRST NEW TOOL! Why do I need to wait this long for some semblance of progression??? Games like The Forest and Subnautica have you progress at your own pace since you can discover new things without an arbitrary wait time. Alright fine, this game has artificial wait times hidden behind the fact that it is a roguelike. Fine. You will need to survive for 9 days (135 minutes) before you have the CHANCE to FIND a satchel so you can finally CARRY MORE THAN TWO ITEMS AT A TIME. YOU DO NOT HAVE AN INVENTORY (other than your two hands) UNTIL 2 HOURS OF PLAYTIME. You will need to survive for 11 days (165 minutes) before you have the CHANCE to FIND a book that lets you BUILD STRUCTURES. This doesn't even matter as far as I can tell for two reasons. 1. The only way to progress is to make several day long trips to various POIs to progress the story. 2. You just unlocked the ability to carry more than two items at a time 30 minutes ago. The game shows every unlockable you can get, the latest is after 20 days (5 hours) of continuous survival. Based on everything I have found so far, I believe I have found the best way to play the game. Step 1: Start a new run. Step 2: Play for 5 hours without dying to unlock everything. Step 3: Die. Step 4: Start a new run and enjoy actually being able to find all of the cool items and tools this game has to offer. I liked what I played and probably would continue to enjoy it. The game is an infuriating time sink to unlock core survival game mechanics. I will not be sinking my time into this however and I will request for my refund.

很有想法的游戏，巨大的开放式地图，基本完整的主线剧情，残酷的生存法则，美丽的热带丛林风貌，出色的天气和物理效果，搭配丰富的装备和食物，让你的海岛放逐生活变得充满趣味，即使通关了主线剧情也会想着继续留在岛上。因为官方将该游戏设定为罗格赖克风格所以死亡直接死档（不能再继续玩，但是可以继承并重开，保留主线进度和装备解锁进度），而且没有多少很有效的回血手段，大部分时候遇敌都是一对多，夜晚还会受到野兽袭击和黑夜伤害，开局难度很大，但是随着游戏的进行，解锁的装备越来越多，主线剧情得到的装备也会显著提升生存质量，加上亟待丰富的建筑系统和可以大量填充内容的巨大地图，这款游戏的潜力将会非常大，官方的持续打磨为这款游戏带来了持续性的升级。很不错的VR生存冒险游戏，推荐入手。 另外，装备的解锁是需要越来越多的生存天数的，全部存档通用，而且随着主线剧情推动到中后期敌人也会有所变化，所以请踏实地在海滩区域生存，多多积累生存装备，不要开局就去看攻略，不要害怕死亡，每一次死亡都会积累生存经验。现在开局可以在浅海找到板条箱了，可以开局就去找找，可以存放不少东西。注意板条箱是没有盖的，所以只要倒过来，东西就全部掉出来了，小心点。PS：用石头砸锁头可以打开箱子，随机开出已解锁的物品。

The game is a roguelike survival that makes you unlock new stuff and mechanics the longer you survive, which by itself wouldn't be an issue if the game was full of new items to discover and craft, but as of now you need to play hours just to unlock the satchel, the only way you have, to carry stuff with you (before getting it you can only carry stuff with your own hands, and that's all), and on top of that it's not even a craftable item, but you need to find it randomly inside of a chest. The crafting is really limited, and available only through a book you unlock after some days of survival. To keep it short, what happens is that you spawn with no ability to craft stuff or even carry stuff with you, you need to do the same things for hours (break a coconut for thirst and food, and make a camp fire to survive the night) just to kill yourself and finally play with some core mechanics that for some reason were unavailable from the start. and on top of that, due to the limited amount of things you can unlock by surviving, the roguelike aspect ends pretty much after just your first run. As a roguelike, it's not well thought. As a survival, it sucks. There are the foundations to make it a proper game, but as of now, the game it's not worth the money.

Even though this game is officially at version 1.0+, it still feels incredibly unpolished. The controls are very clunky, making it a chore to navigate simple terrain like rocks, logs, and other small objects. My biggest issue happened on my second run: I finally made it to the ship on day four, waited for the game to save, and took a break. When I returned, my save was completely missing. I'm sick to my stomach at the wasted time. For a 'Full Release' to have game-breaking bugs like this is unacceptable. I can't imagine going back to the game anytime soon.

I played this game for a few hours and quickly became unhappy with it. Then the game crashed and I lost all my progress as I was close to completing the first chapter, I decided to never play it again. After a few weeks I tried playing it again since there are good things that can be said about it. The visuals are very good and the objects in the game are well crafted. In VR I love the visual immersion and sense of being in a great imaginary space. But the mechanics quickly make me hate the game. Moving is painfully slow. There are bugs were assets disappear. There's a weird grabbing action where sometimes things I put my hand near go flying off into space, which make building fires difficult. Striking rocks together sometimes will never create a spark and you die because no fire is started. Worst is the respawn where every time something kills you, you start back up in the same place as were the game opens for the first time. I've seen the same terrain way way too many times. I have better things to do with my life than be punished by this game.

It's a relatively decent game mechanics-wise, for what it's trying to do, but sadly I cannot recommend it in its current state due to horrendous performance. I have a pretty beefy system and I have no problem running other vr games at 90 fps, even with higher resolution scales. Bootstrap Island, however, cannot maintain a stable framerate, even though it does not look that good, with frequent dips into 50-60 range, which simply does not feel good in VR. I don't think that it's an issue that will be fixed in the future, so be careful if you're planning to buy this.

Played about 5 hours and reached around day 17 without dying. The concept and atmosphere are great, but the actual gameplay loop feels frustrating instead of rewarding. The biggest issue is pacing. Days are too short and movement is slow, so you cannot explore properly without constantly worrying about getting back in time. If you push a bit too far, you get stuck outside at night, and that is where the experience falls apart. Night encounters scale too aggressively. Enemy numbers increase to the point where you are fighting large groups at once, and at that stage it stops being about skill. You can prepare, use fire, try to position yourself, and still get overwhelmed simply because there are too many enemies attacking at the same time. Some enemies also feel overtuned. Even with a pistol, certain enemies take multiple hits to kill, which feels unreasonable when you are already dealing with swarms. When several of them attack together, there is little room for counterplay. Base building does not solve this. It is very resource heavy, and the game does not give you enough time or freedom to gather what you need efficiently. You end up stuck near your base without being able to expand it properly, which slows progression even more. You also need luck just to unlock the "book" randomly in chests. Exploration ends up feeling restricted and repetitive. You move a short distance, stop, secure the area, and repeat. Combined with low early inventory space and important upgrades like the satchel being locked behind luck and time, it becomes tedious instead of exciting. The permadeath system adds tension, but in its current state it feels punishing rather than fair. Losing a run often comes from being overwhelmed by scaling enemies rather than making a clear mistake, which makes the reset feel undeserved. (I understand there is a custom mode where you can disable night monsters, but that feels like avoiding the issue. The base game would benefit more from longer days and reduced enemy spawns, especially when you end up dealing with very large groups.) Overall, the game has a strong foundation, but right now it feels like it is constantly working against the player. The combination of slow movement, short days, aggressive scaling, and limited inventory makes progression feel like a grind rather than a rewarding survival experience. PS: I´d like to hear a responce from the developers since i am just a beginner, and maybe i missed something. I did not mean to criticize, the game is good but this had to be brought up.
